title: A replication fork meets a lesion
summary: Replication forks arrive one after another at a stretch of template with a lesion in it. Say where the forks pile up, how they are spread along the template, and how long it takes for a given share to be stuck.

stages.label: Before the lesion
stages.note: Forks travelling up to the lesion, 0 to 5 kb.

stages.label: Past the lesion
stages.note: Forks that have gone beyond the lesion, 5 to 15 kb.

spec.story: Replication forks reach this stretch of template one after another at a steady rate and travel along it. Each dot below is one fork in a sample of the forks on the stretch.
spec.note: The lecture says which lesions arrest a fork and which do not, not how fast forks move, so the times and distances are illustrative. A gap left in the lagging strand, and a fork being rescued later, are not modelled.

treatments.label: Put a bulky adduct in the leading-strand template
treatments.because: A bulky lesion physically hinders the polymerase, and leading-strand synthesis is continuous, so a fork that meets it in the leading strand template stops there.

treatments.label: Put a UV photoproduct in the leading-strand template
treatments.because: Both UV photoproducts distort the strand on a large scale and arrest the fork, as bulky adducts do, so forks gather in front of it.

treatments.label: Put the same lesion in the lagging-strand template
treatments.because: Lagging-strand synthesis is repeatedly re-primed, so a new RNA primer is laid down beyond the lesion and the fork carries on, leaving a gap behind it.
